skill.name: agy-worker
skill.description: Use when Codex or Claude Code should delegate repository exploration or implementation to Google Antigravity CLI (agy), then review, verify, repair, and deliver the result.
skill.summary: Delegate bounded repository work to Antigravity CLI and retain independent review, verification, and final acceptance.
skill.author: cagdasyurekli

security_audit.summary: Most reviewed alerts are documentation, syntax, or defensive validation rather than malicious behavior. Confirmed risks involve session-mode provider authority, unconfined candidate verification, optional credential forwarding, and disabled Keychain auto-lock. No evidence found for covert exfiltration or audit-directed prompt injection; native grants and 296 unadjudicated capped matches still require review. Static review was capped at 400/696 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 296 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Session provider execution retains ambient user authority.
remediation.suggestion: Use native containment where supported, or a separately isolated account or container. Review ambient hooks and plugins before approving session execution.

remediation.issue: Driver verification executes candidate code without host confinement.
remediation.suggestion: Run checks in an OS-isolated verification environment with restricted filesystem and network access. A disposable copy and snapshot gate are insufficient.

remediation.issue: Credential environment opt-ins reach untrusted verifier code.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid credential-bearing variables during verification. Where required, use disposable least-privilege credentials and restrict outbound network access.

remediation.issue: Dedicated Keychain setup disables automatic locking.
remediation.suggestion: Document bounded automatic-lock settings instead of disabling locking. Require explicit unlock when needed and relock the dedicated Keychain after provider work.

remediation.issue: Native Keychain service grants cannot enforce item-level authentication scope.
remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated account or credential broker exposing only the provider token. Keep broader Keychain operations outside the untrusted provider boundary.

remediation.issue: Native networking permits arbitrary TCP 443 recipients and wildcard listeners.
remediation.suggestion: Apply destination restrictions through an external proxy or firewall. Remove listener grants unless required, and verify loopback-only binding where listeners are necessary.

remediation.issue: Static review was capped at 400 of 696 matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual review of the remaining 296 matches before automatic publication. Preserve the review cap warning until that evidence is available.

semantic_findings.title: Native Network Grants Do Not Restrict Recipients
semantic_findings.description: Native mode permits the bound provider image to contact arbitrary non-local TCP 443 endpoints and bind wildcard listeners. These grants permit unintended destinations or service exposure; they are documented capabilities, not evidence of covert exfiltration.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The generated Seatbelt rule uses remote tcp *:443 without a recipient allowlist. The security guide explicitly documents wildcard listener exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Native Keychain Services Exceed Item-Level Authentication
semantic_findings.description: The provider and security helper receive system Keychain service access. The dedicated file binding does not constrain helper arguments or item operations. Broader same-user credential reads or changes may remain possible, depending on OS permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The profile grants system Keychain Mach services without item-level restrictions. The guide acknowledges broader operations but does not prove access to other credentials.

content.user_title: Delegate Repository Work and Verify Results
content.value_statement: Delegated coding needs clear approval boundaries and independent checks. This skill coordinates Antigravity CLI work, candidate review, bounded repairs, and verification records.
actual_capabilities: Coordinate exploration, task, and project workflows through the bundled runtime.
Preview provider-readable content and bind task settings to a launch approval digest.
Stage selected files in a private Gitless directory and reconcile approved write paths.
Track job status, preserve usable candidates, and support bounded repairs in the same worker conversation.
Bind driver-selected verification evidence to candidate state before finalization.
Offer explicit native containment for supported macOS scoped launches without silent fallback.
limitations: Live work requires Bash, Python 3, Git, an installed AGY CLI, and provider access.
Approved repository content may reach Google/Gemini; scope approval does not guarantee provider privacy.
Session mode and ordinary driver verification retain user authority; disposable worktrees and copies are not security sandboxes.
Native containment requires supported macOS scoped execution and dedicated Keychain setup; offline checks do not prove authentication or correctness.

use_cases.title: Add Focused Regression Tests
use_cases.description: Delegate selected test changes, inspect the resulting diff, and independently run the relevant suite before accepting the candidate.

use_cases.title: Explore an Unfamiliar Repository
use_cases.description: Delegate a bounded architecture investigation while retaining responsibility for source checks, coverage limits, and the final explanation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Project Repair
use_cases.description: Track a broader audit-and-fix job, preserve partial candidates, and return independent check failures for repairs within an approved cycle budget.

prompt_templates.title: Check Local Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agy-worker to check offline readiness for this repository. Report missing prerequisites without starting provider work or changing user configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Bounded Exploration
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an explore preview for the parser and its tests. Show the exact task, readable scope, isolation choices, model settings, and approval digest. Wait for my approval before any provider launch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review exposure before repository exploration.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate a Focused Test Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a task workflow adding parser error-path tests. Limit reads to the parser and direct tests, and writes to those tests. Request my approval for content, isolation, model, and budget before dispatch. Review the diff and independently verify the candidate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement and verify a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Repair Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a scoped project workflow for this approved repair. Bind the exact task, model, isolation, five-cycle limit, and scoped-repair permission for my approval. After approval, use isolated verification and return sanitized failures to the same conversation. Finalize only with candidate-bound evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage repair and verification across multiple attempts.

output_examples.input: Preview selected parser tests before delegating changes.
output: Illustrative preview: parser source and direct tests are provider-readable; only the selected tests are writable.
The exact task, isolation selection, model settings, budget, and launch approval digest are ready for review.
Provider execution is waiting for explicit human approval.

output_examples.input: Review a completed test candidate and report verification honestly.
output: Illustrative result: the driver reviewed the candidate diff and independently ran the selected parser tests.
The focused checks passed; the full application suite was not run.
The workflow records partial verification against the bound candidate, without committing or publishing changes.

output_examples.input: Recover when native authentication is unavailable.
output: Illustrative blocked result: the dedicated provider Keychain is missing or locked.
Provider execution did not start, and isolation was not changed to session mode.
Owner setup or unlock is required before an explicitly approved retry.

best_practices: Approve the exact task, readable content, destination, isolation, model, and budget; request fresh approval when exposure changes.
Prefer small selected-content scopes, keep secrets and controller logs outside them, and use OS isolation for untrusted verification.
Review the actual candidate diff, preserve useful partial work, and finalize with independently collected checks and explicit coverage gaps.
anti_patterns: Treating installation, a successful offline diagnostic, or a worker report as permission to transmit content or proof of correctness.
Using prompt restrictions, disposable worktrees, or selected staging as substitutes for host isolation.
Executing worker-reported commands, silently changing isolation, or replacing failed delegation with unapproved direct edits.

faq.question: Which driver tools are supported?
faq.answer: Codex CLI and Claude Code are supported driver hosts. Antigravity CLI performs the delegated work.

faq.question: Does installation authorize provider transmission?
faq.answer: No. The owner must approve the exact task, content boundary, destination, isolation, model settings, and budget before live dispatch.

faq.question: What is the difference between scoped and whole-worktree dispatch?
faq.answer: Scoped dispatch stages selected readable entries and reconciles an approved write subset. Whole-worktree dispatch exposes every reviewed worktree entry and requires separate explicit approval.

faq.question: Does session mode isolate the provider from my computer?
faq.answer: No. Session mode retains user filesystem and network authority, ambient HOME, and enabled hooks or plugins. Staging does not confine host access.

faq.question: Where is native isolation available?
faq.answer: Native isolation requires supported macOS scoped containment and a dedicated provider Keychain. Unsupported hosts fail rather than silently switch to session mode.

faq.question: How are worker results accepted?
faq.answer: The driver reviews the candidate diff and runs independent checks. Candidate-bound evidence supports finalization; worker command claims alone never establish acceptance.
